title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive text generation capabilities, but their ability to self-correct their reasoning is still uncertain. This paper examines the self-correction capabilities of LLMs, focusing on intrinsic self-correction, where the model corrects its initial responses without external feedback. The results show that LLMs struggle to self-correct their reasoning, and their performance often deteriorates after self-correction.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You think you have the answer, but you're not sure. A Large Language Model (LLM) is like a super-smart friend who can help you with the problem. But, can this friend self-correct its own mistakes without any help from you?

Our research shows that LLMs struggle to self-correct their reasoning, even with multiple attempts.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
We used several LLMs, including GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, to test their self-correction capabilities. We gave them a set of reasoning tasks, such as math problems and common sense questions, and asked them to self-correct their initial answers.

We found that the models' performance often decreased after self-correction, even with multiple attempts.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated the LLMs on several benchmarks, including GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, and HotpotQA. The results show that the models' performance decreases after self-correction, even with multiple attempts.

For example, on GSM8K, GPT-3.5's performance decreased from 75.9% to 74.7% after two rounds of self-correction.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our findings have significant implications for the development of LLMs. If LLMs cannot self-correct their reasoning, it may limit their ability to make decisions and solve complex problems.

This highlights the need for further research into self-correction mechanisms and the importance of evaluating LLMs in a more comprehensive and nuanced way.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our research highlights the importance of intrinsic self-correction, where the model corrects its initial responses without external feedback. We also demonstrate the need for more comprehensive and nuanced evaluation of LLMs.

Our findings contribute to the development of more robust and reliable LLMs.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
You can try experimenting with LLMs and self-correction mechanisms to see how they work. You can use publicly available LLMs and benchmarks to evaluate their performance and explore the limitations of self-correction.

This can help you better understand the challenges and opportunities in developing more robust and reliable LLMs.
